The fire damaged several outbuildings but was contained before reaching the main laboratory complex. No injuries were reported, though local residents were advised to keep windows closed due to smoke. The cause remains under investigation.

The Pirbright Institute is a research establishment, based at Pirbright, that investigates diseases in farm animals. It specializes in viral pathogens, including foot-and-mouth disease and African swine fever. The site operates at the highest level of biosecurity, with containment facilities designed to prevent any accidental release. Scientists there work on vaccines and diagnostic tools, collaborating with global partners to protect livestock and food security. The institute's work is vital for both British agriculture and international trade, as outbreaks can devastate farming economies.

pair.human_continuation:
(A second site at Compton, Berkshire was closed in 2016 with research being transferred to the Pirbright site.) It is one of eight UK research institutes supported by the UK's Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC). The Pirbright site includes international reference laboratories for the diagnosis of livestock diseases exotic to the UK, including the World Reference Laboratory for foot and mouth disease. The site also conducts research on viruses including foot and mouth disease and bluetongue virus.

On Saturday 4 August 2007 it was announced that the strain of foot-and-mouth disease detected in cattle three miles (5 km) away was similar to that in use at the Pirbright site.
